errors.claim: Change initiatives fail at scale because people do not own the change ideas.
errors.source_check: The source asks why change fails "so often," not "at scale," and gives two factors: poor contextual fit and, as an underappreciated second factor, lack of ownership.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "One underappreciated factor in why change fails so often is that people who do not own the ideas will not fully accept them."

errors.claim: The three common org topologies are each a stable region on the OT map.
searches: three common Org Topologies|Resource Topology|Delivery Topology|Adaptive Topology
errors.source_check: The source names three common topologies and depicts them on the map, but never calls them "stable regions."
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "The Primer names three common org topologies: Resource, Delivery, and Adaptive."

errors.claim: Three further premises ground the MADE method.
errors.source_check: After stating that MADE has four steps, the matching source region gives two further propositions: every organization already has a design, and org design comprises elements that can be aligned strategically. The reference likewise lists only two bullets.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Two further premises ground the method."

errors.claim: The "cargo-cult" consequence is borrowed-through evidence because "cargo-cult" is a borrowed term.
errors.source_check: The source uses "cargo-cult" but cites no person, work, or external source for the term. The passage itself is verbatim source content, not a traceable borrowed-through citation chain.
errors.suggested_fix: delete the [BT] marker and its explanatory note; retain the passage as [V].

errors.source_check: The source calls Scrum popular and makes an explicit conceptual mapping to Definition-of-Done completeness, but expresses no approving or endorsing stance.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Neutral conceptual mapping: the horizontal axis corresponds to increasing completeness of the Definition of Done in Scrum."

errors.source_check: The source says kata was adopted into business language and popularized in management via Toyota; it does not express an approving stance toward Toyota.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Neutral provenance connection: the source says 'kata' was popularized in management via Toyota."

errors.claim: Systems thinking is a discipline the practitioner must "practise" [V].
searches: systems thinking|learning the Org Topologies language|hands-on workplace
errors.source_check: The source wording is "This activity requires practicing systems thinking." The quoted word "practise" is neither the source's form nor its spelling.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the verbatim phrase "requires practicing systems thinking," or change the marker to [AP].

errors.claim: SAFe expands to "Scaled Agile Framework" in the source.
errors.source_check: The source explicitly prints "The Scale Agile Framework (SAFe)." "Scaled Agile Framework" silently corrects the source using outside knowledge.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "SAFe (Scale Agile Framework)" or use "SAFe" without expansion.

errors.claim: The source treats SAFe as a neutral framework example.
errors.source_check: The source says that "We are doing SAFe" communicates little and characterizes typical SAFe implementations as interdependent incomplete teams at Tasks level plus fast-flow teams at Capabilities level. That treatment is diagnostic and critical, not neutral.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Diagnostic framework example: the source says the SAFe label communicates little and uses the OT map to expose its typical structure."

errors.claim: The authors explicitly frame against treating Resource Topology or resource utilization as the default org goal.
searches: fit for|one of three|three common|management.s choice
errors.source_check: The source presents Resource Topology as one of three common topologies, explains its limitations, and states when it can be fit for purpose. It never explicitly discusses or rejects it as a "default."
errors.suggested_fix: correct to "Resource Topology is one of three common topologies and is fit for organizations seeking high utilization of rented, defined skills"; delete the default-attribution language.

errors.claim: The authors define a topology as "a stable region on the OT map characterising a set of archetypes."
searches: topology is|topology means|topology characterized|three common Org Topologies
errors.source_check: The source describes and labels Resource, Delivery, and Adaptive Topologies but provides no prose definition using "stable region" or an equivalent formulation.
